summary: Schema-handoff parse backpressure causing long-tail completion and request timeouts in JSON mode
description:
Issue summary: Customer observes intermittent long-tail completion latency and client timeouts when using JSON/structured-output mode with a large schema. Impact: Several production requests (5-10% of sessions during peak) exceed 10s final-chunk latency and cause downstream service timeouts. Environment: dedicated cluster serving Noteable Analytics in us-east-1, pinned to redwood-open-13B model variant with streaming JSON output and schema validation enabled.

Observed behaviour: Most requests complete within SLO (<=500ms tail), but a non-trivial tail of requests stalls at finalization step for 2-20s before the final token is emitted. Clients receive partial streaming chunks then a long silence, then either a final chunk or a connection timeout (504). This happens only when strict schema validation is enabled and the schema includes many optional nested fields (schema size ~120KB).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sample code: create streaming completion with json_schema set to large schema (~120KB) and schema_validation: strict; 2) Send varied prompts that cause deeply nested objects and optional lists to be emitted; 3) Observe streaming trace for final-chunk gap and client-side timeout around 8-12s on a subset of requests; 4) Repeat under load (50-100rps) to reproduce long-tail spikes.

Profiler snippets: incremental JSON-schema validator shows worst-case O(n*m) behavior on highly-branching schemas and large arrays.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:10 - Priya Kapoor: Acked. Reproduced on staging; starting profiling on parser-service to capture CPU/hot functions.
2026-03-11 09:27 - Support (Ana Ruiz): Shared example trace with customer and asked for reduced schema to test impact. Customer confirmed reduced schema removes the long-tail.

2026-03-12 11:02 - SRE (Marcus Li): Observed parser-service instances on node gpu-10 show sustained user CPU at 70-85% during validation. Suspect synchronous full-schema validation is blocking IO loop and delaying final-chunk emission.
2026-03-13 08:45 - Priya Kapoor: Applied temporary account-scoped flag json_validation=lax for Noteable Analytics to mitigate immediate timeouts. Monitoring shows tail reduction to <0.5%.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: 1) Synchronous strict validation of the full JSON schema after tokenization blocks parser-worker thread and accumulates backlog under bursty traffic. 2) Large schema with many optional branches forces backtracking and expensive canonicalization during validation. 3) Interaction between streaming chunk buffering and validation means final token waits until entire object validated. Evidence: profiler traces point to validation functions (validateObject, validateArray) dominating CPU time; removing/shortening schema removes delay in controlled tests. Related PR found in parser repo to improve incremental validation (PR 412).
workarounds_applied:
- Turned on account flag json_validation=lax for Noteable Analytics (temporary)
- Customer advised to reduce schema size and avoid deeply nested optional lists where possible
- Increased client timeout for critical routes to 20s as a safety buffer (temporary)
resolution_notes:
Mitigation: rolled out account flag to avoid strict post-handoff validation that blocked final-chunk emission. Customer confirmed improvement (time-to-final token median reduced from 1.2s to 0.3s, tail reduced significantly).
Next steps: engineering to implement incremental/streaming-friendly schema validation in parser-service so validation can progress concurrently with token streaming; target patch scheduled (parser-service PR 425) and follow-up test plan logged.
Follow-up owner: Priya Kapoor (parser-service team).
next_steps: 1) Deliver parser-service incremental validation (PR 425) and run load tests against large schema scenarios (owner: Priya). 2) Add server-side metric json_validation_queue_latency and expose per-account in Console. 3) Update runbook with guidance to temporarily switch to json_validation=lax and schema size limits. 4) Post-mortem/retrospective in #incidents and Confluence page.
resolution: Mitigated (temporary) - account-scoped lax validation flag enabled; engineering patch in progress
